name: The Pale Enumeration — Nnaji-Brandt Gallery Incident, 2204
creator: Saoirse Nnaji-Brandt (visual artist, geneware practitioner)
description: Artist Saoirse Nnaji-Brandt installed 'The Pale Enumeration' in a Tier 3 gallery on July 19, 2204: 1,440 genetically modified human skin samples — all legally sourced from cosmetic geneware clinics — arranged by modification type, each labeled with the client's Tier classification and the modification's stated purpose. The work made visible the aesthetic hierarchy encoded in elective geneware, and gallery visitors could scan samples with their BCI to hear recorded testimony from the modification recipients. The exhibition was injuncted by Axiom BioInterface on Day 4 for alleged proprietary geneware process disclosure.
medium: physical installation, BCI-interactive, neural feed documentation
cultural_impact: The four days the exhibition was open generated more neural feed discourse than any art event in the preceding decade, and the injunction itself became the artwork's most discussed element — proof of the thesis the piece was making.
controversy: Some modification recipients who had not consented to their samples being publicly displayed sued Nnaji-Brandt; others publicly endorsed the work. The legal status of excised cosmetic geneware as personal property remains unresolved.
story_hooks: Three of the 1,440 samples cannot be traced to any registered geneware clinic — the genetic profiles don't match any known modification protocol.
Nnaji-Brandt claims the full 1,440-sample dataset was backed up before the injunction; Axiom claims to have destroyed it. Someone has been selling high-resolution scans on gray-market feeds.
A character realizes their own modification is in the dataset — which means someone sold their discarded tissue without authorization.
